title: Chicken breast, fried, coated, skin/coating edible

content.title: About
content.content: Fried chicken breast coated in a crispy breading is a staple of fast‑food and restaurant menus. The breast pieces are dipped in a seasoned flour‑egg mixture, sometimes rolled in breadcrumbs, and then deep‑fried until golden. The edible coating adds flavor, crunch, and extra calories.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Breaded fried chicken breast is one of the most popular fast‑food items worldwide.
Traditional breading often includes paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and breadcrumbs for extra taste.
Some establishments double‑fry: a quick deep‑fry followed by a short oven finish for a lighter crust.
Chicken is a lean meat, but frying in oil dramatically increases its caloric density.
Breading can be made gluten‑free using corn starch or rice flour.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It contains niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals: phosphorus and selenium
items.content: Phosphorus is important for bones and teeth, while selenium acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein and fat in the coating helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Calories from the oil and carbs in the breading quickly replenish energy stores.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Deep‑frying and breading make the dish energy‑dense; portion control is recommended.

items.title: Saturated fats and trans fats
items.content: Reused or overheated oil can generate trans fats, which are harmful to heart health.

items.title: Salt and additives
items.content: Breading often contains salt and flavor enhancers, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Standard wheat‑based breading can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella; internal temperature should reach 75 °C (165 °F).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Breaded fried chicken breast is usually served hot as a main dish, in burgers, salads, or with dipping sauces such as barbecue, mayo, or mustard. It pairs well with fries, vegetable sides, or rice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked chicken breast in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in freezer bags at –18 °C; reheat in an oven or air‑fryer to retain crispness.
